key_insight: Multiwavelength excitation photoluminescence can separate interface- and bulk-driven degradation in perovskite solar cells, revealing that PEABF4 initially passivates the ETL/perovskite interface but later accelerates depth-spreading thermal degradation.
engineering_relevance: This provides a nondestructive diagnostic for tracking where recombination losses originate during aging, helping engineers evaluate interfacial treatments and stability strategies more accurately.
method: Multiwavelength excitation PL to probe depth-dependent recombination.
Phenethylammonium tetrafluoroborate (PEABF4) treatment as the model interface passivation strategy.
Diffusion-recombination simulations to interpret wavelength-dependent PL decay in terms of surface recombination velocity and bulk lifetime.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that PEABF4 reduces interfacial recombination losses initially, but after thermal aging the PL decay signatures broaden from the ETL/perovskite interface into the absorber, consistent with worsening depth-dependent degradation.
watch_item: PL-based depth attribution is model-dependent, so separating surface and bulk effects requires careful calibration and may be sensitive to device stack geometry and excitation conditions.
paper_title: Wavelength-Dependent Photoluminescence Mapping of Depth-Dependent Degradation Under Thermal Stress in Phenethylammonium Tetrafluoroborate Treated Perovskite Solar Cells
